claims.text: The target material is a solid-solution high-entropy alloy containing at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 at.% each.
Ti-rich or NbTi-based alloys containing heavy transition metals can provide examples of the proposed starting material with substantial atomic-size variation.
Local lattice distortions caused by atomic-size mismatch govern superconducting transition temperatures and critical fields in the target HEAs.
Replacing size-mismatched atoms with electronically similar atoms having closer atomic radii will reduce atomic-size mismatch and local lattice distortion.
The baseline and modified alloys will be synthesized under identical processing conditions.
Both comparison materials should be homogeneous, single-phase BCC solid solutions.
Atomic-size mismatch induces local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions alter interatomic bond lengths.
Distortion-induced bond-length changes modify the local electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The resulting electronic-structure changes enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Reducing local lattice distortion should lower the superconducting transition temperature.
Reducing local lattice distortion should decrease the upper critical field.
The proposed baseline alloy has composition Nb34Ti33Zr14Ta11Hf8 in atomic percent.
The Nb34Ti33Zr14Ta11Hf8 baseline has a superconducting transition temperature of approximately 7.5 K.
The Nb34Ti33Zr14Ta11Hf8 baseline has a high upper critical field.
Nb34Ti33Zr14Ta11Hf8 is a type-II superconductor with intermediate electron–phonon coupling and an upper critical field of 12.2(1) T.
The proposed mechanism applies only when substitutions preserve similar electronic structure and leave lattice-distortion magnitude as the principal changed variable.
Substantial changes in carrier density or additional scattering centers could invalidate the proposed distortion-mediated interpretation.
Direct quantitative correlations between local lattice distortion and electron–phonon coupling in these alloys are not well established.
The hypothesis would be falsified if a verified reduction in local distortion produced no measurable decrease in Tc, upper critical field, or another electron–phonon-coupling indicator.
